accountDeletion.title: Delete account
accountDeletion.intro: This page explains how to delete your RookHub account and what happens to your data.
accountDeletion.introPartner: Your account here is a RookHub account (same sign-in details). This page explains how to delete it and what happens to your data.
accountDeletion.inApp: The button below opens the “Delete account” card in your profile – if you are not signed in, you sign in first. By hand: ☰ → Account → Profile, at the very bottom. Confirm with your password there. The account is deleted immediately.
accountDeletion.inPartner: You can delete the account only in RookHub: sign in there (same details) and go to ☰ → Account → Profile, at the very bottom “Delete account” – or use the button directly. Confirm with your password; the account is deleted immediately, for this site too.
accountDeletion.backup: Deletion takes effect immediately and cannot be undone. Save what you want to keep first: courses, repertoires and games can be downloaded one by one as PGN – in the course, in the repertoire list (⋮) and in each game (⋮).
accountDeletion.removed1: Your identity and personal data (username, email, display/real name, FIDE/ChessResults ID, Chess.com/Lichess name, Discord link) and login access.
accountDeletion.removedCourses: Your own courses (imported or created yourself) – also for everyone you shared them with: shares, group access and other people's learning progress in these courses go with them.
accountDeletion.removed2: Personal content and links: repertoires, tournament subscriptions/favourites, friendships and group memberships.
accountDeletion.removedGames: Saved games including scoresheet photos and reconstructions, game analyses, point game runs, analysis jobs, calculation trees and remembered positions.
accountDeletion.removedShared: Worksheets and your share links: links to shared games, lines, reconstructions and worksheets (including the QR code on the printout) no longer open.
accountDeletion.removedKids: Your KidHub progress (levels, stars, courses) – KidHub uses the same account.
accountDeletion.removedConnections: Connections and settings: API tokens (RepCheck or the browser extension loses its connection immediately), Chessable access, Lichess and your own engines, push notifications, messages with the admins and notifications.
accountDeletion.removedLeague: LeagueHub: open import drafts of the club database, including half-finished ones.
accountDeletion.kept: Aggregated solving/play statistics (e.g. solved puzzles) are retained in anonymised form that cannot be traced back to you.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: RookHub is a chess training platform (puzzles, endless mode, courses, repertoires). This policy explains how personal data is processed under the GDPR.
privacy.introLeagueHub: LeagueHub (part of RookHub) prepares lineup forecasts for team matches and keeps the game database of participating clubs. The account is the same as on RookHub. This statement explains how personal data is processed under the GDPR.
privacy.introClubHub: ClubHub (part of RookHub) is the club's card index for its children and young players. The account is the same as on RookHub. This statement explains how personal data is processed under the GDPR.
privacy.clubIntro: In ClubHub, the club's management and trainers keep a card for each child or young player. A card is not an account: the child does not need to be registered with us.
privacy.clubData: Stored on a card: first name (required), last name, date or year of birth, level, FIDE ID and national player ID, the child's groups, optionally a photo with a marked face area for the portrait, and dated trainer notes on learning progress.
privacy.clubContacts: Contacts: phone numbers and e-mail addresses, each with a note such as “mother” or “father”.
privacy.clubAttendance: Attendance per training session (present or absent), the topic and content of the session, and photos of the session.
privacy.clubAccess: Only signed-in club accounts with the matching role see the card index: management sees everything, trainers only the children of their own groups. Nothing of it is reachable without signing in; the server logs contain only ID numbers, no names.
privacy.clubPhotos: Whether photos of children may be taken and stored is agreed between the club and the parents; ClubHub does not record a consent.
privacy.clubLink: A child's own RookHub account is linked to its card only with a one-time code that the account itself redeems. The club then sees summarised training figures (puzzles, training goals, KidHub progress), no individual attempts. Both sides can remove the link.
privacy.clubRetention: The data is stored on the operator's server and is not cached on the device. Deleting a card removes its contacts, notes, photo and attendance. If a trainer's account is deleted, the cards and notes stay with the club, without the trainer's name.
privacy.kidIntro: KidHub is the chess site for children. Here we explain in simple words which data we store and why. The detailed version for parents follows below.
privacy.kidDevice: Without an account, your stars and your progress stay only on this device. We do not store them.
privacy.kidAccount: With an account, we store your progress in your account so you can keep playing on another device. It is the same account as on RookHub. When you log out, the progress is removed from the device but stays in the account.
privacy.kidParents: Please only create an account with your parents’ permission. Parents can have the account deleted at any time — a message to the address below is enough.
privacy.kidNoTracking: KidHub shows no ads, uses no tracking cookies and has no chat. To choose a suitable language, we check once which country your internet address comes from — it is not stored for this.
privacy.kidVisibility: Other logged-in RookHub users can find your username. So pick a nickname, not your real name.
privacy.kidLogs: Our server notes which pages are opened — with your username if you are logged in. This is deleted after 90 days.
privacy.kidPeriods: How long we keep what is listed below under “Retention & deletion”.
privacy.kidDetails: For parents: the following sections describe in detail which data we process. The KidHub account is the same account as on RookHub, so they apply to both sites.
privacy.controllerNamed: The controller responsible for data processing is the operator of this website, reachable at:
privacy.leagueIntro: LeagueHub helps members of participating chess clubs prepare for team matches in their leagues (Tyrol, Bavaria). Each club has its own club database that no other club can see. For this we also process data of players who have no account with us and whose data we do not collect from them directly (Art. 14 GDPR).
privacy.leagueClub: You are currently using LeagueHub for {{club}}.
privacy.leagueSourcesPairings: pairings, results and team rosters from chess-results.com and from the league manager of the Bavarian Chess Federation
privacy.leagueSourcesGames: games from Lumbra’s GigaBase, the ChessBase Mega Database and the chess-results.com game database
privacy.leagueSourcesClub: club games uploaded by members or submitted without logging in via a share link (also as a scoresheet photo, see “AI services”) — players of the uploading club appear in them only under the club’s name by default; their real name is stored internally for that club’s own analyses and is never displayed or passed on (if the replacement is deselected for a side when uploading, the real name is stored visibly)
privacy.leagueSourcesOnline: public games of online accounts on Lichess and chess.com. To fetch these, our server sends the usernames of these accounts to the respective platform; chess.com is operated by a US provider (transfer to a third country). Unlike for the weekly “games” goal, the games themselves are stored here.
privacy.leagueData: Categories: name, FIDE ID, club, rating and appearances according to the rosters; games and opening profiles calculated from them; a calculated probability of being lined up in a round (a model trained on previous seasons); online accounts on Lichess and chess.com that we assign to a player — from public profile information (such as real name and country) or entered by club officials, marked as “confirmed” or only presumed — together with a comment on the assignment and the public games of these accounts.
privacy.leagueBasis: Purpose and legal basis: preparing for team matches; legitimate interest of the club and its members (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). The data comes mostly from publicly accessible sources.
privacy.leagueRecipients: Recipients: logged-in accounts with LeagueHub access (the club group and administrators). Via a share link, anyone who has the link sees the shared match without logging in: the roster with predictions, player cards, opening trees and games of the players listed there — online accounts only if they are considered “confirmed”. A share link is valid until seven days after the round (for a round already played, seven days from sharing; without a known round date, 30 days) and can be revoked earlier.
privacy.leagueRetention: Retention: league data, games and profiles are kept as long as LeagueHub is operated, because the predictions are based on previous seasons. People who upload via a share link are not recorded by name — for the upload limits we only keep a check value (hash) of the IP address. For scoresheet photos it serves the daily limit and therefore remains after the reading has been accepted or discarded; after two days it is cleared the next time someone uploads a scoresheet without an account. For submitted game lists it remains until the list has been imported or discarded; a draft left open is deleted after 30 days without changes, the next time the drafts are opened. Scoresheet photos are deleted when the reading is accepted or discarded (details under “AI services”).
privacy.leagueObjection: Objection: you can object to the processing of your data in LeagueHub at any time (Art. 21 GDPR) — a message to the address under “Contact” is enough. We will then in particular remove the assignment of your online accounts and your data from LeagueHub, unless compelling legitimate grounds for the processing prevail.
privacy.dataIntro: Depending on your use, we process:
privacy.dataAccount: Account data: username, email address, password (stored only as a hash).
privacy.dataProfile: Profile data (optional): display/real name, FIDE ID, ChessResults ID, Chess.com/Lichess username, optional Discord link.
privacy.dataUsage: Usage data: solved puzzles, endless/course progress and statistics, play rating, login timestamps.
privacy.dataTechnical: Technical data: IP address, browser and device, requested addresses with timestamps and a visitor identifier in the server logs — when you are logged in, with your username (details under “Server logs”).
privacy.dataIpCountry: KidHub (the kids' site): if your browser language is not one of its languages, the country of your IP address is determined to choose one — locally on our server with the country list of DB-IP (IP Geolocation by DB-IP, CC BY 4.0). The address is not passed on or stored for this.
privacy.dataScoresheet: Photos of scoresheets, if you have a game read in — with everything on them, such as both players’ names, the event, the date and signatures.
privacy.purposes: Providing the account and features (performance of a contract, Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) as well as operational security, error analysis and reach measurement via logs (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
privacy.visibilitySearch: User search: any logged-in account can find you — by your username, your display name or your Chess.com or Lichess name (part of the name is enough), and by the beginning of your FIDE ID or ChessResults ID. The result shows these details as far as you have entered them in your profile.
privacy.visibilityLeaderboards: Leaderboards: logged-in accounts see your display name there (without a display name, your username) together with your figures.
privacy.visibilityFriends: Friends: only once a friend request has been accepted does the friend see your puzzle statistics, the puzzles you failed (“Revenge”) and your tournament history.
privacy.visibilityGuests: Without logging in, your profile cannot be viewed.
privacy.messages: If you write to the admin team or it writes to you, we store the messages with their time. They can be read by you and by every account allowed to handle messages — the administrators and people they have given this task. We delete read messages after 365 days; unread ones remain until they are read; all of them go with your account.
privacy.push: If you turn on push notifications, your browser’s push service issues a delivery address (Google for Chrome, Microsoft for Edge, Mozilla for Firefox, Apple for Safari), which we store with your account. Our server sends every notification through this service; its content is encrypted, and the service only sees the delivery address, time and size. Some of these providers are based in the USA (transfer to a third country). If you turn push off, delete your account or the service reports the address as invalid, we delete it.
privacy.thirdIntro: Data is not sold. Depending on your use, the following services are involved:
privacy.thirdDiscord: Discord: only on voluntary account linking (Discord ID/name) for display in the RookHub Discord bot.
privacy.thirdChessresults: chess-results.com: tournament data is fetched server-side when you set a ChessResults ID or load tournaments.
privacy.thirdChesstools: api.chesstools.org: when you search for a player in the FIDE rating list (for example in your profile or for the tournament history), our server sends the name you entered (last name, first name) to this service and receives matching entries of the FIDE list. Your IP address and your account are not transmitted.
privacy.thirdChesssites: Chess.com / Lichess: if you store a username for these platforms in your profile, our server queries their public game APIs automatically — in the background every 6 hours by default while a weekly “games” goal is active for you, and whenever you trigger a manual sync in the training goals. Your username on that platform is transmitted to it; chess.com is operated by a US provider (transfer to a third country). We only store the number of your rapid/classical games per day and the time of the most recently fetched game — no game moves. Removing the username in your profile stops these queries.
privacy.thirdLogging: Elasticsearch/Kibana: self-hosted logging/monitoring on our infrastructure.
privacy.thirdPush: Push services of the browser vendors: only if you turn on push notifications — details under “Push notifications”.
privacy.thirdHosting: Hosting: operated on our own server infrastructure with a TLS reverse proxy.
privacy.thirdAnthropic: Anthropic PBC (USA): reads scoresheet photos with its AI model Claude — details under “AI services”.
privacy.thirdTextLlm: Language-model server (NVIDIA DGX Spark, Austria): writes game recaps, explanations of mistakes, roasts and course translations and processes questions for “Ask the comments”; the server is run by the operator of this website, the data is not passed to any third party — details under “AI services”.
privacy.aiScoresheet: Reading a scoresheet (in RookHub via “Read a scoresheet”, in LeagueHub for club games — there also without logging in via a share link): the photo is sent to Anthropic PBC in the USA, whose AI model Claude transcribes the moves and header data. This is a transfer to a third country. Reading runs through a Claude account of the operator; whether and how long Anthropic stores the data and whether it uses it to improve its models depends on the terms and privacy settings of that account. There is no data processing agreement with Anthropic. The legal basis is performance of a contract for you (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and, for other people on the scoresheet, the legitimate interest in recording games played (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). On our side, in RookHub the photo stays with the game until you delete it (if reading failed, for 30 days). In LeagueHub it is removed from the reading as soon as the reading is accepted or discarded; until then the club’s administrators can also see the reading including the photo. After that we keep the photo together with what the recognition read and the accepted game for 365 days to improve the reading (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) — it can be seen by the operators and, for correcting the game later, by whoever uploaded it and the club's administrators; it is then deleted automatically, and immediately with your account. A reading left open with an account keeps the photo until you delete it or your account; a reading without an account (share link) that is never accepted is cleared after 14 days. Without a photo, nothing is sent to Anthropic.
privacy.aiLocal: Game recaps, explanations of mistakes and “Roast my game” never run via Anthropic, but on a separate language-model server (NVIDIA DGX Spark) in Austria run by the operator of this website. The game data is sent there over an encrypted connection, for recaps and roasts including the players’ names and ratings. The data is not passed to any third party. “Ask the comments” (the text of your question) and course translations run on the same server; translations only involve course texts (comments, line titles, chapter names), no information about you.
privacy.botIntro: If you use our Discord bot, it also processes:
privacy.botDmLog: Direct messages: what you write to the bot and what it sends you is stored with a timestamp, shortened to 300 characters per message; personal account-linking links are made unrecognisable. The bot deletes entries older than 30 days the next time it saves. Only the bot’s admins and moderators can view them (for troubleshooting).
privacy.botActivity: Motivation messages (/motivation): the bot evaluates your Discord status “Playing …” only if you are subscribed — you sign up yourself, or an admin or moderator signs you up. If a game other than chess has been running there for at least an hour, it may send you a reminder to train by direct message. For this it remembers the game name and start time while the game is running. You can unsubscribe at any time with the bot command /motivation, option “aus” (off).
privacy.botLogs: Logs: every command sent to the bot is logged with your Discord ID and name, server and channel (or “direct message”), the shortened command parameters and the result, as are reactions to bot puzzles for the statistics. For motivation messages, the Discord name, game name and playing time are recorded — of the message itself only its length, not its content. These logs are kept month by month in our self-hosted Elasticsearch; there is currently no automatic deletion period for them.
privacy.tournamentIntro: For the tournament views in RookHub and on the tournament site, our server fetches public tournament data from chess-results.com and stores it in a separate database:
privacy.tournamentData: Data: the tournament (name, venue, dates, rounds), players with name, title, FIDE ID, rating, country, team and board, as well as pairings and results — including people who have no account with us. With “Look up clubs”, the server also looks up the club for FIDE IDs in other tournaments on chess-results.com.
privacy.tournamentRetention: Retention: we delete fetch jobs 30 days after they finish, and a looked-up club assignment 180 days after it was last refreshed. Tournaments with their players, pairings and results are currently kept without a fixed time limit, because RookHub refers to them.
privacy.logsIntro: Our server logs every request in order to find errors, fend off abuse and count usage. An entry contains:
privacy.logsContent: IP address, browser and device (user agent), the requested address with time and result, and a visitor identifier. If you are logged in, your username and your user number are included in plain text — so the identifier is not pseudonymous. Without logging in, it is the random identifier your browser creates for puzzles without an account.
privacy.logsEmail: When we send you an email (for example to reset your password), your email address and the subject appear in the log.
privacy.logsAccess: The logs are kept in our self-hosted Elasticsearch; only the operator can view them. They are not passed on and not used for advertising.
privacy.logsRetention: They are deleted automatically after 90 days (at the latest one week later). If you delete your account, entries already written remain until the end of this period.
privacy.storage: We do not use tracking cookies. Browser storage (localStorage) holds e.g. your login token, settings and — if enabled — offline puzzles. These remain on your device.
privacy.storageLogout: When you log out, we remove from the device what belongs to your account, such as cached content and local progress. Device preferences such as language, board, theme, interface size and e-ink mode remain. Solutions not yet sent also remain and are only sent at the next login of the same account.
privacy.retention: Account data is stored until you delete your account. You can delete your account at any time — identity and personal data are removed, anonymised statistics are retained. More:

holes.help:
The hole finder walks through your repertoire and, in every position where your opponent is to move and you have prepared a reply, asks the Lichess explorer what is played there.

A hole is an opponent move that is played at least as often as the threshold and leads to a position that appears nowhere in your repertoire – not even via another move order.

Holes are sorted by how often you reach them in real games. The end of a line is not a hole.

Lichess.org allows only about 15 lookups per minute, so the first run over a large repertoire takes a while; RookHub remembers positions it has already looked up, and a stopped search picks up where it left off. The local database has no such limit.
holes.thresholdHelp: The share of games in a position from which a missing opponent move counts as a hole. 1% also finds sidelines, 5% only the main moves. Allowed: 0.1 to 50%.

maia.hint:
Maia-3 is a neural network from the University of Toronto. It has learned from millions of games which moves people of a given playing strength choose — including their typical mistakes.

The strength corresponds to a Lichess blitz rating; as a rule of thumb it is about 200 points above FIDE Elo.

Maia does not calculate ahead but plays by feel. The engine stays off meanwhile so that you do the calculating yourself.

“Report bad moves”: after each of your moves the engine checks in the background whether the evaluation dropped by at least 0.2 pawns — then a note appears, and “Analyse” shows you what was better. “Keep the evaluation bar”: the bar next to the board keeps showing the evaluation during the sparring; lines and arrows stay hidden.

help.title: Help & Guide
help.subtitle: Everything you need to know about RookHub – step by step.

p: RookHub is your central chess portal: puzzle training (standard, endless, daily puzzle), book courses and repertoires, the point game, your own games with engine review, worksheets, personal training goals, plus profile and friend features – all in one place. Tournaments have their own tournament site.

Much of it works without an account (puzzles, analysis, daily puzzle, point game). Sign in for personal progress, your games, friends and training goals – you then start on the dashboard, whose tiles you choose via “Customize”. Every area is reachable through the ☰ menu (grouped into Training, Analysis & collection, Community and Account); this page explains them – use the table of contents to jump directly.
You can register with a username and password; an email address is optional. Use “Register” in the top bar to create an account, then sign in with the same credentials.
Tick “Stay logged in” at login to remain logged in for 90 days instead of 30. You can sign out any time via ☰ → Account → Logout.
In your profile you set your display name and your links: FIDE ID, ChessResults ID, chess.com and Lichess usernames. These connect RookHub to your external chess accounts.
If you store your ChessResults ID, upcoming tournaments are subscribed for you automatically. Your chess.com and Lichess names are used for the play tracking of your training goals.

Use the player search (by last and first name) to find yourself in ChessResults/FIDE and adopt the right ID directly. Your public profile shows others only a reduced view – without your real name, ChessResults ID or Discord.

If the chess bot is active in your Discord, you can link your RookHub account to Discord. The bot sends you a link with a token; if you are logged in the link is established immediately, otherwise after your next sign-in.
Once linked, you appear in daily-puzzle and Weekly-Post leaderboards with your Discord name, and the bot can show you your training progress. You can unlink it again any time in your profile.
Beyond linking, everyone is welcome in our Discord community — join at https://discord.gg/wczc4BJtMf to chat, ask questions and follow announcements.
On the “Friends” page, you can search for other users and send friend requests. Incoming requests appear on the “Requests” tab where you can accept or decline them.
Only the recipient of a request can confirm it. Existing friendships can be removed at any time.

Tournaments – live data from chess-results.com, subscriptions, favorites and the round monitor – have their own tournament site. Signed in, you open it via ☰ → Community → Tournaments; your login is carried over.
The standard puzzle mode gives you tactical problems from a large pool. You play the solution right on the board; correct and wrong moves are reported instantly.
Puzzles can be filtered by theme. When logged in, your progress including puzzle Elo is saved – without login you can still practice, but progress stays local on the device.
After solving (or giving up) a puzzle, tap the heart to keep it; your collection is under ☰ → Training → Favorites, ready to replay or analyse.
In endless mode you solve a continuous series of increasingly harder puzzles until you make too many mistakes. You set the starting Elo, themes, fast-track thresholds and Stockfish depth yourself.
Your high score and finished runs are saved; see the history under ☰ → Account → Puzzle History and archive old runs.
Every day (by UTC) there is a fixed daily puzzle that is the same for everyone – so you can compare directly.

After solving you see the leaderboard of all solvers. A “solver” is anyone who solves the puzzle on the first attempt. If you are linked with Discord, your name also appears in the bot's Discord embed.
Courses are imported chess books you work through puzzle by puzzle. Which books you see depends on your group access; administrators see all of them.
You choose between book order (sequential) and random order. Your progress is saved per book and shared across both modes; you can reset a course's progress.
The “Courses” menu item only appears once at least one book has been granted to you.
In ☰ → Analysis & collection → Catalog, you see the courses and repertoires others have made available to you, and can “Request” individual ones.

The Weekly Post mirrors the weekly chess-bot posts: a game or study with a date that you play through puzzle by puzzle. Via a post's link, reading and playing through also work without login; progress and the leaderboard only count signed-in attempts.
“Done” means you have played all puzzles (solved or not). Giving up or resetting after a move counts as a failed attempt. A live leaderboard shows all participants.

Set one daily training-time goal (in minutes) plus weekly goals for games played (rapid/classical) and full training days. Coaches can provide a default per group; your personal goal takes precedence.

The tracker colors each day by goal completion (none/partial/full) – the daily status comes from your training time (puzzles, courses, Chessable and logged offline activity), while playing is a weekly goal.

RookHub fetches rapid/classical games automatically from Lichess and chess.com (public, no login there). Use “Update playing time” to trigger it immediately. Bullet, blitz and correspondence do not count.
Your puzzle Elo curve and further analysis of your solved puzzles over time are under ☰ → Account → Statistics.

By default, analysis runs in your browser via Stockfish (WebAssembly) – also offline. You get several main lines (MultiPV), evaluations for any position and an opening explorer. Analysis works without login; on first start the browser engine downloads about 7 MB once.

Signed in, you can add a stronger engine in your profile under “External engine” (e.g. one registered on your Lichess account) and compare two engines. With “Analyse in the background” (in the ⋮ menu of the position) you queue a position for the background engine; the results are listed under “Analysis jobs”.
Repertoires are collections of PGN files (opening/middlegame/endgame) you upload and manage. You can add files via drag & drop, download them and fetch the combined PGN (max 10 MB per file).
With the optional RepCheck browser extension, your opening repertoires are checked right on chess.com and lichess.org analysis pages (see “Browser extension (RepCheck)”).
RookHub is a Progressive Web App: you can install it as an app and use much of it offline. Puzzles, the endless pool, whole books and the Stockfish engine are pre-cached.
Puzzles solved offline are queued and synced automatically once you are back online. An Android install guide including the APK is under ☰ → Account → Install app.

Theme: without an account you switch between light, dark and system theme directly in the ☰ menu; signed in, you choose it in your profile under “Appearance”. Language: ☰ → Language (signed in: ☰ → Account → Language) – RookHub speaks 25 languages and your choice is saved.

In your profile under “API tokens” you create personal tokens for tools that access RookHub on your behalf. RepCheck usually fetches its token itself via “Connect to RookHub”; a manually created token (scope “extension”) is the fallback. The raw token is shown only once at creation – copy it immediately.
Tokens have a scope and an optional expiry date and can be revoked at any time.

RepCheck highlights, on chess.com and lichess.org analysis pages, the move at which your game leaves your stored opening repertoire. The repertoire stays on the server – the extension only sends the current game’s move list and gets the deviation back.

RepCheck is a browser extension, available in the [Chrome Web Store]({{chromeUrl}}) and as a [signed Firefox add-on]({{firefoxUrl}}). Besides the repertoire check it saves games to RookHub, brings your Chessable courses over and keeps positions via “Remember line”.

Setup: in the extension popup choose “Settings” → “Connect to RookHub” – RepCheck opens RookHub, waits for your sign-in and creates its access token itself. Entering a token by hand (created under “API tokens” in your profile, scope “extension”) remains as a fallback.
Source code, version history and details on [GitHub](https://github.com/kahalm/repcheck).
You reach the imprint and privacy policy via the respective pages. You can delete your account yourself: identity and personal data are anonymized, while the anonymized statistics are kept (GDPR).

Found a bug or have a wish? “Feedback / Report a bug” in the footer takes you straight to the issue tracker on GitHub; questions are also welcome in our Discord community (☰ → Community). Without an account, ☰ → Info opens the quick-start overview.
In the point game you guess an analysed game move by move: you take one side, play your move and get points at once – measured against the move that was actually played, rated by the engine.

The “Master games” are open to everyone, even without an account; there you play the winner's side. Signed in, you can also play your own games under “Your own analyses” and choose the side – add a game as PGN and it is analysed in the background.

Your games are under ☰ → Analysis & collection → Games – saved with the RepCheck extension on chess.com or lichess, added via “Upload PGN” or read from a scoresheet photo. “Analyse game” computes it in the background – afterwards the evaluation curve with accuracy and move classes appears under the board. You can also share a game via link or download its PGN.

“Read a scoresheet”: take a photo of your scoresheet; an AI model (Claude by Anthropic, USA) reads the moves, RookHub checks every move on the board and stores the game in your games. You fix uncertain moves via “Review and correct”. The number of scans per day is limited.

Write down what you still remember of a game – the first moves, single positions, short move sequences – and close the gaps step by step. “Close the gap” searches for move sequences leading from one part to the next; a suggestion only becomes part of the game once you confirm it.
“Share whole game” creates a link to the game including its open gaps; whoever opens it needs no account.

With “Send to worksheet” you collect positions from a course, a chapter or after a solved puzzle; they land on the clipboard. From there you print a sheet with several diagrams per page and room for the solution – or save it as a PDF.

Once shared (“Share this sheet (link + QR code)”), a sheet gets a link that is also printed as a QR code: whoever opens it can play the sheet through on the board without an account. Note: the solutions are behind the link too.
The leaderboards under ☰ → Community → Leaderboards show who solved the most puzzles, endless runs, course lines and daily puzzles this week, this month or overall.

Chessable courses come to RookHub via the RepCheck browser extension (see the RepCheck section) – it runs in your own, signed-in browser. Importing through RookHub itself is switched off: Chessable blocks data-centre IPs, and that pattern can get your Chessable account locked.

With “Remember line” in RepCheck you keep a position from chessable.com; you find it under ☰ → Analysis & collection → Remembered, where you can analyse it or queue it for background analysis. Your active training time on chessable.com counts towards your training goals.

The e-book library holds chess books as PDF, EPUB, DJVU and comic archives. PDFs open right in the browser: scroll through the pages, zoom, and jump back to where you stopped – the page you were on is remembered per book. Other formats are downloaded.

Anyone signed in can upload a book and decide who sees it: only you, one of your groups, or all signed-in users. The uploader (and admins) can edit title, author, year and tags, change the visibility later or delete the book.

The Woodpecker Method (Smith & Tikkanen) trains tactical pattern recognition by solving the same puzzles over and over, faster each time. Pick one or more courses and start a training – the rules are fixed as in the book.

Cycle 1: you have four weeks to solve as many puzzles as you can, in course order; they become your set. You may backdate the start – what you solved in these courses since then counts. After at least one day off, each further cycle brings the same set in random order and has half the time (14, 7, 4, 2, 1 days). Only your first attempt per puzzle counts in a cycle. You are done once you solve the set within one day, or after the 7th cycle.

profile.nameHelp:
The tournament history looks you up on chess-results, and it searches by NAME — there is no lookup by number there. Without a last name this site cannot show you a history.

The display name is what other people see. Your login name is never shown.
profile.identityHelp:
Two people can share a name, and the search by name returns both. A FIDE ID or a chess-results ID decides which of them is you.

Without one, the history shows every tournament of everyone with your name — and you will notice, because there will be tournaments in it you never played.

The data comes from chess-results, and it is looked up by NAME — so your last name has to be in your profile. A FIDE ID or chess-results ID decides which of your namesakes is you; without one, tournaments of other people with your name appear here.

Results are fetched one tournament at a time and kept afterwards. The first look at a long history therefore fills up gradually.

woodpecker.title: Woodpecker
woodpecker.intro: The same puzzles again and again, each time in half the time – after the method by Smith and Tikkanen.
woodpecker.rules:
Cycle 1: four weeks – solve as many puzzles as you can, they become your set.

Then at least one day off. Each further cycle: the same set in random order, in half the time (14, 7, 4, 2, 1, 1 days).

Only the first attempt per puzzle counts in each cycle. Done when a cycle takes one day or less, or after cycle 7.
